events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.00 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered ride (F6, F8), so deviation distance feeds the fare directly and RD-2 requires a per-segment refund of the extra km on any segment not excused by RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F6][RD-1][RD-2]. The record shows one off-route segment, 12:12–12:16, 2.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.80 km, adding 2.13 km [F3], and the trace settles that no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch exists, so RD-4(a) exemption fails; the speed bands on AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY and JURONG TOWN HALL ROAD (F9, F10) are at most corroboration and cannot exempt on their own [F3][F9][F10][F11][RD-4].

No exemption applies to that segment. There is no in-app chat at all between rider and driver [F7], so no rider message sent before 12:12:15 exists that could be consent [F3][F7][RD-5]. The driver's statement ("I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted") was written after the trip and is a claim, not rider consent, and even taken at face value it is the driver's own navigation choice, not a rider agreement [F8][RD-5]. No stop was measured in the segment, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt it and no rider-named place exists in the record [F3][F7][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts as an unexempted deviation under RD-1/RD-2 [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount: the per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare over distance km: $15.14 ÷ 10.74 km = $1.40968.../km [F6][RD-2]. Applying the trace formula only to the segment's extra km, 2.13 km × $1.4097/km = $3.0027, rounded to cents = $3.00 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. The trace's own figure for the corridor-level excess ($3.26 on 2.31 km, F4) covers unsegmented corridor mileage which RD-2 expressly does not refund; only the measured segment is refunded here [F4][F6][RD-2].

Because the case is established against the driver and the profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days (F14), RD-6 requires the account-review flag on top of the refund; the profile is used only for that additional action, not to establish the deviation itself [F14][RD-6].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your route complaint and you're getting $3.00 back.

One part of your trip went off the best route: about 2.13 km more than needed on that stretch, and nothing excused it — no traffic incident on the road taken, no stop you asked for, and no message from you approving that route. Because your ride was metered, that extra distance added to your fare.

The $3.00 covers just that extra distance on your fare. It comes as a Ryde voucher on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route dispute on this trip and found one off-route segment.

It added about 2.13 km over the best route. Nothing excused it: no traffic incident on the road you took, no rider-requested stop, and no rider message approving that route. Your note that the GPS rerouted you is your navigation choice, not rider consent. Since your ride was metered, that distance added to the fare.

$3.00 goes to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Separately, your account is being sent for review given prior upheld route disputes. The notice on that review tells you what happens next.
